history.summary: DUPLICATE FLAG: this CSV row is the same temple as seq 1036 (id lakshmi-narayan-bari-kailashahar) - the 1964 Krishnananda Sevayet founding, Tripura royal family assistance, and Tamal tree details match exactly. Per the Tripura government Unakoti district newsletter, the Laxmi Narayan temple at Kailashahar was established in 1964 by Sevayet (caretaker) Krishnananda and constructed with financial assistance from the Tripura royal family; a Tamal tree was planted in front of the temple by the Sevayet about 60 years ago in honour of Krishna's association with the Tamal tree in the Bhagavata legend. Janmashtami and Durga Puja are celebrated annually with great reverence. CONFLICT FLAG: travelsetu.com claims a 17th-century origin and royal-family construction, which contradicts the 1964 founding documented by the district government - the 1964 date is the better-sourced one.

name: Lakhi Narayan Bari (Laxmi Narayan Temple)
town_description: Kailashahar is the headquarters town of Unakoti district in northern Tripura, on the banks of the Manu river near the Bangladesh border. It is known for the ancient Unakoti rock-cut Shaivite shrines nearby, the Lakshmi Narayan temple, and a mixed Bengali-tribal culture.

travel.airport: Maharaja Bir Bikram Airport, Agartala (~180 km by road; verify)
travel.railway: No station in Kailashahar; nearest major station Dharmanagar (~30 km, verify)
travel.road: Within Kailashahar town; reachable by bus/taxi from Agartala and Dharmanagar

visitor_information.best_time: October-March (cooler, post-monsoon); Janmashtami and Durga Puja are the main festival periods
visitor_information.opening_hours: 5:00 AM - 9:00 PM daily per travelsetu (verify locally)
